Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 6-7.

Using Outsiders at the Table

Outsiders are Source-born beings with old grievances, practical survival needs, and a natural ability to endure divine pressure. Treat them as patient factions, uneasy allies, specialists, rivals, or predators rather than automatic servants.

Their long view matters. Many Outsiders have watched gods rise, fall, and repeat the same mistakes. They often prepare, wait, and act only when the leverage is good.

Loyalty Hooks

  • Protection: an Outsider may serve a god who can keep them alive.
  • Fear: a stronger god can force obedience, but coerced service creates future enemies.
  • Dominion affinity: some Outsiders are drawn toward gods whose Dominion matches their nature or needs.
  • Price: service is often transactional, especially when the Outsider has a specific appetite, craft, or debt in play.
  • Refusal: some Outsiders reject ownership entirely and punish anyone who tries to claim them.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF page 8.

Propaganda

Gods, theologies, and Outsider factions all push stories that justify how Outsiders should be treated. The four common stances are useful as NPC agendas or faction tags.

  • Cattle: Outsiders are resources to control, weaponize, and discard.
  • Enemy: Outsiders are existential threats to destroy before the Descending Storm worsens.
  • Equals: Outsiders are peers with wisdom, power, and claims to respect.
  • Mistakes: Outsiders are failed Source experiments to be used or erased.

Visibility

Outsider appearance ranges from nearly human to openly monstrous. Modern fashion, body modification, costuming, and social denial can help them pass, but those tools work unevenly and can fail under scrutiny.

GM prompt Decide which propaganda frame dominates the local pantheon, then decide which Outsiders benefit from that story and which ones are endangered by it.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF page 9.

Why Outsiders Stay Close

Outsiders risk mortal contact for reasons that are both practical and emotional. These motives are good starting points for contacts, complications, and faction clocks.

External Motivations

  • A god requires mortal-facing servants who can run errands, watch territory, or act without obvious divine spectacle.
  • An Outsider is exiled, hunted, or hiding something important in the noise of a city.
  • Basic needs such as food, water, shelter, money, and access to mortal comforts pull them toward human infrastructure.
  • Addiction, debt, or a taste for mortal experiences creates pressure that supernatural power does not solve.

Internal Motivations

  • Long-lived Outsiders can still be lonely and may use temporary mortal relationships to keep despair at bay.
  • Scholars and lore keepers immerse themselves in human society to study culture, ethics, and technology up close.
  • Some Outsiders are raised among humans and only later learn what they are, creating identity conflicts that may never fully resolve.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 10-12.

Daily Pressure Points

When Outsiders live near mortals, ordinary life becomes a constant risk-management problem. Housing gives them a place to drop disguises. Food may be mundane, symbolic, or horrifying. Money pushes them toward jobs, crime, barter, or patronage. Transport and law enforcement add exposure risk, while technology offers anonymity, delivery, communication, and surveillance all at once.

Methods of Mingling

  • Magical: illusions and glamours are powerful but can drop when concentration breaks or violence starts.
  • Physical: surgery, filed horns, false teeth, contacts, masks, makeup, and concealing clothes help some Outsiders pass, often at a psychological or social cost.
  • Nonphysical: cover stories, costuming spaces, festivals, LARP events, and mortal rationalization can explain away visible oddities.

Sideline Influence

Some Outsiders avoid direct contact and work through businesses, proxies, online identities, bribery, blackmail, compulsion, or disposable mortal agents. These networks are useful as clues: suspicious ownership chains, too-clean accounting, sudden cash, and witnesses who fear an unseen employer.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 13-15.

Communities

Outsiders gather by kin, need, goal, or shared danger. The Descending Storm and the rise of new gods force more of them out of hiding, which increases pressure on territory, secrecy, and old truces.

Haven Types

  • Industrial centers: technology, commerce, weapons, Relic development, and inhuman invention.
  • Art and media centers: adoration, performance, predation, glamour, and hidden patronage.
  • Stonehenge: a gateway to a verdant otherworld that some Outsiders treat as sanctuary or hunting ground.
  • Underground networks: subway tunnels, sewers, hidden markets, sleeping areas, raves, and neutral exchanges.
  • Wilderness reserves: remote habitats where elemental, predatory, or isolationist Outsiders can thrive away from mortal attention.

Scene seed A neutral underground market has stayed peaceful for years because every faction benefits from it. A new god's territory claim threatens to break that balance.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 15-18.

Conflict States

Outsider peace is often only the pause before the next conflict. Wars can target other Outsiders, mortals, gods, territory, resources, reputations, or ancient injuries.

Common War Triggers

  • Blood feuds and inherited grudges.
  • Insults against heritage, honor, or ancestry.
  • Property destruction, theft, or stolen sacred objects.
  • Subterfuge, sabotage, and long-running schemes.
  • Territory invasion or disregard for boundaries.
  • Torture, mutilation, or predation for pleasure.

Conflict Roles

Outsiders at war commonly become assassins, feeders, informants, prisoners, warriors, or weapon dealers. During fragile peace they may become guardians, healers, pest hunters, negotiators, traders, or market enforcers.

Peace Tools

Negotiations, truces, pacts, bribes, gifts, and neutral markets can hold factions together for a while. They are rarely clean. Every deal should answer who benefits, who is excluded, and what happens when someone disrupts the peace.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 19-42.

Many Variations

This chapter is a bestiary-style catalog of Source-born Outsiders. Use these entries as ready opposition, uneasy allies, vassal candidates, faction leaders, territory complications, and payoff sources after divine interaction.

The table below preserves the usable source data without reproducing the chapter text wholesale. Each entry lists the PDF viewer page, threat tier, vassal value, core combat stats, skill dice, named powers, payoff, and a short table-use summary.

Threat Bands

  • Warrior: practical battlefield threat, usable as a single strong foe or recurring ally.
  • Master: major supernatural actor whose powers reshape scenes, factions, or territory.
  • Grand Master: severe mythic threat; usually a session centerpiece or campaign-level complication.
  • Squad: a group or distributed threat, usually stronger when treated as a territory hazard.

Next build step These entries should become actor-compendium documents once the target Part-Time Gods actor schema is verified in this module context.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 21-24.

Ahuitzotl to Catoblepas

Ahuitzotl

  • PDF: 21. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 2.
  • Core stats: Threshold 14, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 8, Defense 5, Initiative +7, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Deception, Influence, Knowledge, Stealth.
  • Powers: Aquatic, Attention-Seeking, Prehensile Tail.
  • Payoff: Aquatic or Extra Arms, flavored as the tail-hand.
  • Use at the table: Waterline broker and ambusher who can lure victims, represent water-bound Outsiders, or negotiate with gods who need an aquatic agent.

Basilisk

  • PDF: 21-22. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: no standard vassal value.
  • Core stats: Threshold 9, Armor 1, Spark 1, Fragments 3, Attack 4, Defense 6, Initiative +8, Damage +0 plus toxic damage.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Intuition, Perception, Speed, Stealth.
  • Powers: Aura of Burning Decay, Small Immortality, Toxic Ambush.
  • Payoff: Toxic immunity for the Puck-Eater and a touch-based Sickened effect for the Scene.
  • Use at the table: Hidden poison hazard, illicit magical pet, or trap-creature whose terrain and concealment matter more than raw force.

Black-Eyed Children

  • PDF: 22-23. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: N/A.
  • Core stats: Threshold 6, Armor 0, Spark 3, Fragments 6, Attack 0, Defense 4, Initiative +5, Damage +0.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Empathy, Influence, Intuition, Perception, Survival.
  • Powers: Immortality, Judgment, Mark of Death.
  • Payoff: Otherworldly Sight or immunity to one Child's Judgment for the Scene.
  • Use at the table: Moral pressure encounter and omen of death, especially when wicked mortals or a god's mortal attachments are exposed.

Camazotz

  • PDF: 23-24. Tier: Master. Vassal: 4, with Spark 3 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 18, Armor 2, Spark 3, Fragments 6, Attack 12, Defense 9, Initiative +8, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Discipline, Intuition, Perception, Speed, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Death's Blood, On Vampire Wings, Soul's Connection.
  • Payoff: On Vampire Wings for the Session.
  • Use at the table: Death-linked negotiator, healer, messenger, or blood-drinking ally whose harm can draw nearby kin into the conflict.

Catoblepas

  • PDF: 24. Tier: Master. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 16, Armor 4, Spark 1, Fragments 2, Attack 8, Defense 10, Initiative +5, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Fortitude, Influence, Might, Speed, Survival.
  • Powers: Ruins Left Behind, Toxic Breath.
  • Payoff: Immunity to poison or physical AR +2 from scales.
  • Use at the table: Slow-moving ecological disaster that damages points of interest and creates territory cleanup problems even after combat ends.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 26-32.

Centaurs to Gargoyles

Centaurs

  • PDF: 26. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 2.
  • Core stats: Threshold 9, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 8, Defense 9, Initiative +8, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Empathy, Influence, Medicine, Perform, Speed, Survival.
  • Powers: Divine Power, Martial Training.
  • Payoff: First Move or Divinely Skilled (Marksman).
  • Use at the table: Social, athletic, and martial Outsiders who fit challenge scenes, archery duels, revels, and wilderness faction pressure.

Defilers

  • PDF: 26-27. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 3, with Spark 2 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 10, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 12, Defense 10, Initiative +5, Damage +3.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Fortitude, Knowledge, Survival, Tech.
  • Powers: Destroying Beauty, Straightforward.
  • Payoff: Natural Weapons (Talons) or Bane (Beauty).
  • Use at the table: Saboteur and destroyer of art, beauty, and knowledge; good for attacks on landmarks, archives, monuments, and beloved NPCs.

Dryads

  • PDF: 27-28. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 12, Armor 1, Spark 3, Fragments 6, Attack 7, Defense 8, Initiative +9, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Crafts, Empathy, Influence, Fortitude, Knowledge, Medicine, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Enchanting Beauty, Green Thumb, Home Tree.
  • Payoff: Leaf-like transformation and Aura of Influence (Awe).
  • Use at the table: Seductive plant-spirit whose home tree turns a location into a moral and tactical anchor.

Encantado

  • PDF: 28-29. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 12, Armor 0, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 5, Defense 8, Initiative +7, Damage +0.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Deception, Empathy, Influence, Perception, Speed, Travel.
  • Powers: Pink Dolphin, Trail of Sickness, Weather Control.
  • Payoff: Aura of Influence (Awe) or the Pink Dolphin power.
  • Use at the table: Party-going trickster, romantic predator, weather curse, or spreading sickness tied to a territory grid.

Flesh-Eating Tree

  • PDF: 29-30. Tier: Squad. Vassal: N/A.
  • Core stats: Threshold 30, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 12, Defense 10, Initiative +6, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Deception, Empathy, Fortitude, Perception, Survival.
  • Powers: Central Trunk, Nourishment, Root System, Whispers.
  • Payoff: Whispers or Telepathy.
  • Use at the table: Forest-scale hazard; branches act as extensions, while the hidden trunk is the true objective.

Gargoyles

  • PDF: 31-32. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 2.
  • Core stats: Threshold 15, Armor Stoneskin, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 9, Defense 8, Initiative +6, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Crafts, Discipline, Fortitude, Medicine, Perception, Stealth, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Elemental Lashing, Reinforce Structure, Stoneskin, Stonespeak.
  • Payoff: AR 2 and either Flight or Natural Weapons (Claws).
  • Use at the table: Patient guardian, living architecture, or territorial protector who can repair and reinforce structures.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 32-36.

Headless Horsemen to Nunnehi

Headless Horsemen

  • PDF: 32-33. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 11, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 11, Defense 8, Initiative +8, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Discipline, Perception, Speed, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Mystic Sight, Relentless Tracker, Summon Ride.
  • Payoff: +4 Survival (Tracking) or Summon Ride.
  • Use at the table: Paid hunter, bounty tracker, or relentless consequence for criminals, debtors, and missing-person plots.

Kitsune

  • PDF: 33. Tier: Grand Master. Vassal: 3, with Spark 3 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 18, Armor 1, Spark 4, Fragments 8, Attack 11, Defense 10, Initiative +10, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Deception or Knowledge, Influence, Medicine, Speed.
  • Powers: Fox or Friend?, Generational Trickery, Nine Tails of Power.
  • Payoff: Beast Form (Fox) or hidden Spark for the Scene.
  • Use at the table: Trickster, mentor, manipulator, or hidden elder whose age roll can make the encounter sharply more dangerous.

Manticores

  • PDF: 34. Tier: Grand Master. Vassal: 4.
  • Core stats: Threshold 18, Armor 2, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 14, Defense 10, Initiative +10, Damage +3.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Discipline, Fortitude, Speed, Might, Perception, Stealth, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Bloodfury, Predator's Roar, Spine Spray.
  • Payoff: Aura of Influence (Fear) or Bane (Manticore).
  • Use at the table: Apex predator and god-hunter; best when the players know it has their scent and must decide what bargain or trap is worth attempting.

Mongolian Deathworm

  • PDF: 35. Tier: Squad. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 15, Armor 1, Spark 1, Fragments 2, Attack 7, Defense 8, Initiative +6, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Fortitude, Intuition, Stealth, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Acid Spit, Burrowing, Energy Plating.
  • Payoff: Acid Spit or Armored (Energy).
  • Use at the table: Burrowing swarm threat, black-market monster, or livestock epidemic that spreads unless contained quickly.

Nunnehi

  • PDF: 36. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 3, with Spark 2 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 13, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 8, Defense 10, Initiative +9, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Empathy, Perception, Stealth, Survival.
  • Powers: Divine Warrior, Faster than the Eye, My Home, Simple Illusions.
  • Payoff: +2 Battle checks or +1 Journey Manifestation.
  • Use at the table: Home-territory defenders who punish divine trespass and fight far above their weight inside claimed locations.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 37-42.

Pegasus to Wyverns

Pegasus

  • PDF: 37. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 4, only after worth is proven.
  • Core stats: Threshold 15, Armor 1, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 8, Defense 9, Initiative +9, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Empathy, Fortitude, Intuition, Speed, Travel.
  • Powers: Airborne, Fearless Steed.
  • Payoff: Flight from sprouting wings.
  • Use at the table: Earned companion, aerial advantage, or test of heroism rather than a simple mount purchase.

Perytons

  • PDF: 38. Tier: Warrior. Vassal: 2.
  • Core stats: Threshold 12, Armor 1, Spark 1, Fragments 2, Attack 7, Defense 8, Initiative +7, Damage +1.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Athletics, Perception, Perform, Stealth, Survival.
  • Powers: Flight, Mortal Form, Seemingly Docile.
  • Payoff: Flight or Natural Weapons (Antlers).
  • Use at the table: Roadside predator, wilderness missing-person threat, or infiltrator after a recent kill.

Sphinx

  • PDF: 38-39. Tier: Grand Master. Vassal: 5, with Spark 4 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 25, Armor 2 physical and 3 mental, Spark 5, Fragments 10, Attack 8, Defense 12, Initiative +8, Damage +3.
  • Skills: 5 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Discipline, Empathy, Influence, Intuition, Knowledge, Stealth, Survival, Tech.
  • Powers: Mental Resistance, Tethered, Unquestionable.
  • Payoff: Divinely Skilled (Knowledge) or the answer to one question.
  • Use at the table: Site-bound guardian of a threshold, relic, labyrinth, or answer that should be earned by solving rather than fighting.

Thunderbird

  • PDF: 40. Tier: Master. Vassal: 3.
  • Core stats: Threshold 8, Armor 2, Spark 4, Fragments 8, Attack 10, Defense 14, Initiative +9, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Empathy, Influence, Intuition, Knowledge, Speed.
  • Powers: Create Storms, Shoot Lightning, Shapeshift.
  • Payoff: Unobscured Eyes or Wings.
  • Use at the table: Rural storm-maker and aerial striker whose weather can alter perception, ranged combat, and mortal panic.

Trolls

  • PDF: 40-41. Tier: Master. Vassal: 2.
  • Core stats: Threshold 14, Armor 3, Spark 2, Fragments 4, Attack 9, Defense 9, Initiative +3, Damage +3.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Fortitude, Influence, Might, Perform, Tech.
  • Powers: Effective Attacks, Physically Impressive.
  • Payoff: Natural Armor 2 with rocky, mossy transformation.
  • Use at the table: Night-shift brute, enforcer, or ambusher whose knockback and durability make the battlefield matter.

Weavers

  • PDF: 41-42. Tier: Master. Vassal: 4, with Spark 3 requirement.
  • Core stats: Threshold 9, Armor 1, Spark 3, Fragments 6, Attack 9, Defense 7, Initiative +12, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 4 dice; Athletics, Crafts, Deception, Perception, Speed, Stealth.
  • Powers: Fate Shaping, Feeding, Unleash the Brood, Web-Spinning.
  • Payoff: Extra Appendages (Arms) or +2 to one Manifestation.
  • Use at the table: Fate-bending arachnid manipulator, social predator, and web-terrain controller.

Wyverns

  • PDF: 42. Tier: Grand Master. Vassal: 4.
  • Core stats: Threshold 21, Armor 1, Spark 3, Fragments 6, Attack 13, Defense 10, Initiative +4, Damage +2.
  • Skills: 3 dice; Athletics, Fortitude, Perception, Survival, Travel.
  • Powers: Barbed Tail, Breathing Divine Fire, Time Fluctuations, Sense Territory.
  • Payoff: Sense Territory or Armored (Fire).
  • Use at the table: Territory-seeking disaster; a Wyvern should threaten the grid directly and escalate if not confronted fast.

name: 03. Birthed by the Source: Character Creation

text.content:
Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 43-45.

Birthed by the Source

This chapter adapts Outsiders as playable characters. The procedure follows the normal Part-Time Gods creation flow, but Step One chooses an Outsider Kin, Step Three can use an Outsider Outlook instead of a mortal Occupation, and later steps add special handling for size, passability, diluted Spark, and Outsider attachments.

Creation Steps

  1. Kin and Powers: choose one Outsider Kin and record its Skills, Free Time, Wealth, size, passability, Dominion if any, Blessing, Curse, and available Truths.
  2. Archetype: choose one Archetype normally.
  3. Outlook or Occupation: choose an Outsider Outlook, or choose a normal Occupation if the character can function in mortal society.
  4. Attachments: spend 5 points on Attachments, with the Outsider-specific caveats below.
  5. Finishing Touches: spend Skill or Manifestation points, record Spark 1 and 2 Fragments, then place Bonds, Landmark Bonds, and Worshippers on the Territory Grid.

Special Notes

  • Dominion: some Outsiders start with a Dominion and use the finishing rules for Dominions and Manifestations.
  • Blessings and Curses: Kin powers are playable versions of the antagonist abilities and may be reduced or delayed so the concept works at the table.
  • Available Truths: each Kin has a limited thematic list of Truths that can be purchased with Attachment points or XP.
  • New Outsiders: entries marked with an asterisk are new to this book; unmarked entries reference Outsiders that also appear in the core Part-Time Gods material.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 46-52.

Kin: Camazotz to Dryad

Camazotz*

  • Skills: Empathy +1, Might +1, Perform +1, Stealth +1, Travel +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 3/0. Size: Large, Exposed. Dominion: Death.
  • Blessing: Creature of the Night grants Death, kin telepathy, monstrous natural weapons, flight, night bonuses, and blood-feeding recovery.
  • Curse: Ravenous Soul forces soul-devouring opportunities and links nearby ally damage back onto the Camazotz.
  • Truth options: armored, bane, bat form, colossal size, divine skill, first move, regeneration, unobscured eyes.

Centaur*

  • Skills: Athletics +1, Crafts +1, Marksman +1, Speed +1, Tech +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Large, Exposed. Dominion: Nature.
  • Blessing: Forest Guardian grants Nature, hoof natural weapons, bow-focused divine skill, multi-target archery by sacrificing Pantheon Dice, and a Level 3 glen Landmark Bond.
  • Curse: Anti-Civilization penalizes scenes away from nature and shifts territory interests toward the map edge.
  • Truth options: bane, horse form, beast tongue, first move, healing hands, otherworldly sight, telepathy, unobscured eyes.

Devourer

  • Skills: Fighting +1, Intuition +1, Medicine +1, Perform +1, Survival +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Average, Exposed or temporary Flawless. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Live to Eat turns consumed flesh into Well-Fed Conditions that power First Move, Regeneration, damage reduction, healing, fragment recovery from divine flesh, predatory bonuses, Vassal levels, disguise, and biting through material.
  • Curse: Eat to Live adds Self-Destruction, lowers maximum Bonds, and can destroy Attachments when hunger and Attachment Strain collide.
  • Truth options: armored, fear aura, colossal size, divine skill, extra appendages, natural weapons, unobscured eyes, visions.

Djinn

  • Skills: Crafts +1, Deception +1, Discipline +1, Fortitude +1, Intuition +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 0/2. Size: Average, Passable or temporary Flawless. Dominion: variable.
  • Blessing: Malleable Existence supports shapeshifting into people, animals, or objects, and allows choosing and reallocating a Dominion and Manifestations scene by scene.
  • Curse: My Master Beckons replaces part of Step Four with a Level 3 Master Individual Bond tied to the Djinn prison and mandatory wishes.
  • Truth options: any Truth that fits the Djinn's long history and current role.

Dryad*

  • Skills: Crafts +1, Empathy +1, Influence +1, Medicine +1, Survival +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 2/1. Size: Average, Exposed. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Child of Nature grants awe, wild speech with plants and animals, a Level 3 Home Tree Landmark Bond, teleportation to the tree, tree-based healing, and plant-life commands through Pantheon Dice or Fragments.
  • Curse: Deforestation ties Dryad health and the surrounding territory to the Home Tree's Strain or destruction.
  • Truth options: armored, aquatic, extra appendages, fertility, flight, otherworldly sight, regeneration, telepathy.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 54-57.

Kin: Dwarf to Jikininki

Dwarf

  • Skills: Athletics +1, Fighting +1, Fortitude +1, Knowledge +1, Tech +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Average, Passable. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Forge Mastery grants divine skill in a craft specialty, +3 Relic Levels, a Level 2 Forge Landmark Bond, and rules for investing Fragments or Permanent Fragments into created Relics.
  • Curse: Material Cravings creates Overwhelmed Conditions from frivolous spending and forces Discipline checks to resist interesting purchases.
  • Truth options: armored, bane, divine skill, extra arms, heat immunity, otherworldly sight, regeneration, visions.

Encantado*

  • Skills: Deception +1, Empathy +1, Influence +1, Perception +1, Travel +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 2/1. Size: Average, Flawless, Passable, or Exposed. Dominion: Weather.
  • Blessing: Down By the River grants aquatic movement, divine social skill, human and pink dolphin forms, and magical fertility.
  • Curse: Trail of Sickness weakens most Attachments and spreads Sickness Conditions to mortals or pantheon members who remain close.
  • Truth options: awe aura, beast tongue, first move, flight, disease or sickness immunity, soothing aura, tongues, unobscured eyes.

Gorgon

  • Skills: Athletics +1, Influence +1, Medicine +1, Perception +1, Stealth +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 2/2. Size: Average, Passable or Exposed. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Medusa's Daughter grants uncovered perception skill, poison immunity, serpent-bite poison after grapples, and Stone Gaze against mortals or Sparked targets.
  • Curse: Green Intentions penalizes uncovered social interaction, makes exposed snakes dangerous, and can strain Attachments after close scenes.
  • Truth options: awe or fear aura, beast tongue, empathy or stealth skill, natural weapons, regeneration, soothing aura, telepathy, tongues.

Jikininki

  • Skills: Deception +1, Medicine +1, Might +1, Perform +1, Stealth +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Average, Exposed, Passable, or Flawless depending on mask state. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Borrowed Lives lets the Jikininki eat the dead to assume their form, gain temporary skill levels, alter Free Time and Wealth, retain surface knowledge, and persist as a spirit if the body is slain.
  • Curse: Corruption Shines Through draws animal hatred, imposes fear in battle, and makes beast attacks more dangerous to the mask.
  • Truth options: fear aura, knowledge skill, first move, flight, lash, natural weapons, regeneration, visions.

Source: Outsider's Guide, PDF pages 59-64.

Kin: Kitsune to Nunnehi

Kitsune*

  • Skills: Crafts +1, Deception +1, Intuition +1, Marksman +1, Perception +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Average, Flawless or Passable. Dominion: Trickery.
  • Blessing: Path of the Nine Tails grants Trickery, free fox form, hidden Spark while a fox, and tail-based bonuses as Spark increases.
  • Curse: Crack in the Mask limits human-form duration, makes mask damage reduce passability, and restricts Bonds and Attachment aid.
  • Truth options: aquatic, divine skill, healing hands, lash, regeneration, telepathy, unobscured eyes, visions.

Manananggal

  • Skills: Discipline +1, Empathy +1, Intuition +1, Medicine +1, Speed +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 1/2. Size: Average Flawless, or Small Exposed for 1 Fragment. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: We Only Come Out At Night makes blood the primary healing path, grants a prehensile tongue, a hidden feeding method, a night-only split flying form, natural weapons, fear aura, combat bonuses, and a Level 2 safehouse Landmark Bond.
  • Curse: Half-Body adds Morbid and makes the separated lower body a severe vulnerability until regenerated at the safehouse.
  • Truth options: bane, beast form, extra heads or arms, healing hands, otherworldly sight, soothing aura, telepathy, tongues.

Minotaur

  • Skills: Fighting +1, Fortitude +1, Knowledge +1, Might +1, Survival +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 2/1. Size: Large, Exposed. Dominion: none.
  • Blessing: Walking Powerhouse grants divine Might, natural weapons, stronger Sprint bonuses, close-range armor pressure, temporary impossible lifting, and +4 levels for Bonds or Vassals tied to what the Minotaur protects.
  • Curse: Lost in the Labyrinth slows territory movement and can cause the beast within to attack everyone nearby under stress.
  • Truth options: armored, bane, beast tongue, colossal size, divine skill, bullet immunity, weapon break, visions.

Ningyo

  • Skills: Discipline +1, Intuition +1, Perform +1, Speed +1, Travel +1.
  • Free Time/Wealth: 0/3. Size: Average, Flawless or Exposed. Dominion: none.

Step Four: Attachments

  • Bonds: Outsiders spend Bond points normally, but the player should explain how each Bond fits a life lived around secrecy, hidden places, community obligations, or mortal integration.
  • Truths: Outsiders do not receive the usual free Truth during this step. They may buy only Truths listed for their Kin unless another rule expands the list.
  • Vassals: Outsiders may ignore minimum Spark requirements when taking other Outsiders as allies.
  • Worshippers: Chosen Ones may carry a Kin Blessing, feeding Outsiders strain Confidants harder, and Temple Keepers give non-Dominion Outsiders a general x1 roll bonus instead of a Manifestation bonus.

Step Five: Finishing Touches

  • Outsiders with a Dominion: gain the Skills and Manifestations tied to that Dominion type, but not its Attachments, Blessings, or Curses. Then spend 10 Skill points and 6 Manifestation points, and choose one Skill Specialty and one Manifestation Specialty.
  • Outsiders without a Dominion: repeat the Skill gains from Kin, Archetype, or Outlook, then spend 10 Skill points and choose three Skill Specialties.
  • Size: Small gives Stealth +2, Speed +1, Might -2. Average has no change. Large gives Might +2, Fortitude +1, Stealth -2.
  • Passability: Flawless has no Curse. Exposed uses Complete Mayhem when mortal panic draws attention. Passable uses The Mask Slips when the Outsider's true nature briefly becomes obvious.
  • Base Spark: playable Outsiders start at Spark 1 with 2 Fragments.

Spark and Territory

  • Diluted Spark: Outsiders gain 2 Fragments per Spark instead of a god's usual value, but recover up to 3 Fragments at the beginning of each Session.
  • Divine Regeneration: they may spend 1 Fragment to recover either 2 Health or 1 Psyche.
  • Resisting Manifestations: they may spend 1 Fragment to resist manifestations, gain +1 to those resistance checks, and ignore Condition penalties. Non-Dominion Outsiders can use territory bonuses for these resistance checks.
  • Sensing: they use Sense Spark like gods and have Spark Reaction to flee when a god enters a Scene.
  • Pantheon Pool: full pantheon members add to the pool normally. Allied Outsiders who have not joined get a personal pool like Hoarder dice and cannot share it.
